profile.description: Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank PJSC, together with its subsidiaries, provides banking products and services in the United Arab Emirates and internationally. The company operates in five segments: Retail Banking, Private Banking, Corporate and Investment Banking, Investments and Treasury, and others. It offers current, savings, call, Islamic deposit, business, and money transfer accounts; debit, credit, and corporate cards; auto, car, home, business, and personal loans; and safe deposit lockers. The company also provides Islamic banking retail business finance; wealth management, managed funds, trading securities, and mutual funds; financial education services; cash management; and trade finance services. In addition, it offers Commercial Banking Financing Solutions, such as Insta Finance, POS receivable, construction equipment, professional equipment, medical equipment, commercial vehicle, two-wheeler, construction, lease rental, commercial property, retail business, small and medium enterprise financing, infrastructure and asset finance, and government and public enterprises financing. Further, the company provides working capital solutions; term finance; investment banking; and financial markets solutions; asset management, brokerage, and fund management activities; central treasury operations, and currency and commodity derivative services. In addition, it offers transaction processing and back-office support, trust, and engineering services; Treasury financing services; Data classification and analysis services; and marketing consultancy, as well as involved in private banking; and developing, investing, leasing, and managing real estate properties. The company was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Abu Dhabi, the United Arab Emirates. Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank PJSC operates as a subsidiary of One Hundred and Fourteenth Investment Company LLC.

summary: Q2 2026 profit before tax surged 26% YoY to record AED 3.83B, marking ADCB's 20th consecutive quarter of profit growth.
First-half profit before tax climbed 28% to AED 7.61B; net loans grew 10% while cost-to-income ratio improved 90bps to 26.8%.
Management forecasts loan growth reaching high teens by end-2026, up from 10% in H1, with stable net interest margins expected.
Non-interest income rose 22% in H1, reaching 38% of total income as bank targets 40%; progressive dividend policy maintained.
Shares fell 1.25% to $14.18 amid margin pressure concerns; NIM compressed to 2.2% in Q2 due to competitive deposit market conditions.
